summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of COPD, diastolic heart failure, obesity hypoventilation syndrome, and atrial fibrillation was admitted for dyspnea and hypoxia. She presented with acute on chronic heart failure, evidenced by weight gain, leg edema, elevated BNP, and pulmonary congestion on imaging. Treatment with IV diuresis led to clinical improvement, with resolution of hypoxia and stabilization of kidney function. Her oxygen was carefully titrated to avoid hypercapnia, and she continued to refuse CPAP therapy. She was transitioned back to oral diuretics, discharged on home oxygen, and given strict fluid and weight monitoring instructions. Follow-up was arranged with her primary care provider and heart failure clinic.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Patient's other noncompliance with medication regimen
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
